You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

content.text:
Clinical history (case record; may contain prior observations):
age: 36
gender: male
history: A 36-year-old man presented with chronic productive cough and history of recurrent lower respiratory infections. Physical examination was unremarkable. The patient was non-smoker with no occupational or environmental exposure to respiratory irritants. There was no family history of a similar illness. The results of blood analysis were within normal limits.

Based on the chest X-ray findings in Figures 1a and 1b, which diagnosis is most consistent with the observed radiological features and the patient's clinical presentation?
A) Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
B) Normal aging
C) Mounier-Kuhn syndrome
D) Williams-Campbell syndrome
E) Sarcoidosis
F) Pulmonary tuberculosis
